title: Targeting HNF1A-mediated therapeutic resistance in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma is exceedingly aggressive and refractory to conventional and targeted
therapies, including those directed at mutant KRAS-signaling (hyperactivated in >90% of cases); but the
underlying mechanisms that determine therapeutic response/resistance—including pancreatic cancer stem
cells—are poorly understood, and effective strategies to overcome therapeutic resistance are unavailable.
These studies will mechanistically explore the regulation of the novel pancreatic cancer stem cell driver,
HNF1A, define a strategy for targeting HNF1A using BET-inhibitors and specific depletion of BRD4, and
assess the efficacy BET-inhibitors/BRD4-ablation in overcoming HNF1A-mediated resistance to targeting
KRAS-signaling and pancreatic cancer stem cells. The data generated from this proposal will identify a
clinically viable strategy to target HNF1A-dependent pancreatic cancer stem cells, overcome resistance to
KRAS-targeting strategies, and improve outcomes for patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

title: Multidisciplinary Training in Alzheimer and Related Dementias
text:
The Washington University T32 training grant “Multidisciplinary Training in Alzheimer and Related
Dementias” (ADRD-T32) is designed to prepare the next generation of researchers in Alzheimer disease
and related dementias. The program provides training in collaborative, multidisciplinary research for
predoctoral and postdoctoral trainees from a variety of disciplines, emphasizing translational research and
utilization of large scale NIH-supported data sets.

title: Targeting Epigenetic Heterogeneity in Pediatric T cell leukemia: Epi-Clones as Drivers of Chemoresistance
text:
This proposal aims to uncover the genetic and epigenetic mechanisms underlying chemotherapy resistance and
relapse in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), focusing on the role of distinct tumor subpopulations, or
epi-clones, that drive disease progression. Using cutting-edge single-cell and in silico technologies, we will in-
vestigate the clonal evolution of T-ALL and identify novel therapeutic targets to overcome chemoresistance. By
targeting key regulatory factors and chromatin-binding proteins that govern epi-clones, this work has the potential
to significantly improve treatment outcomes for T-ALL patients.

title: Regulatory mechanisms linking protein synthesis and degradation
text:
The balance between protein synthesis and protein degradation is a critical component of cel-
lular health, and protein level imbalance can promote the development of cancers and age-related
diseases. The work in this proposal will determine mechanisms through which cells attenuate
protein synthesis when protein degradation is compromised, illuminating the regulatory networks
that maintain this important balance of protein levels. The results could advance our understand-
ing of how cellular pathways are affected by protein degradation inhibitors, an important class
of chemotherapeutic drugs, and thus provide rationale for potential, future improvements to such
treatments.

title: Microglial-derived extracellular vesicles as biomarkers in traumatic brain injury
text:
Traumatic brain injury (TBI) imposes a significant societal burden due to high disability and mortality and currently
lacks effective treatments. Inflammation driven by brain cells called microglia is believed to play a critical role in
TBI pathology, and understanding this process could yield improved therapies. My project evaluates novel
technology to noninvasively monitor microglial activity after TBI, potentially enabling personalized treatment,
enhancing clinical outcomes, and broadly advancing brain health in various neurological conditions.

title: 11-Oxyandrogens and Aging: Health Implications
text:
The adrenal glands produce androgen precursors, which are known to be important during fetal and early
development. Recent data suggest that a set of unique adrenal androgens, called 11-oxyandrogens, might play
important roles in aging individuals. The proposed research aims to deeply characterize the patterns of 11-
oxyandrogens in aging men and women, and to derive associations between 11-oxyandrogens and various age-
related health outcomes, including bone, metabolic, cardiovascular, and general wellbeing.

title: Toward Translation of an Immunotherapeutic Nanomedicine for Neuroblastoma
text:
Neuroblastoma is an aggressive pediatric cancer with a poor prognosis despite an intensive multimodal
treatment regimen. This proposal aims to advance an experimental immunotherapeutic nanomedicine toward
clinical translation through optimization of physiochemical and biological properties, rigorous preclinical
evaluation in animal models of neuroblastoma, and optimization of combination immunoregimens.

title: The Role of Granular Acidification in the Pathogenesis of Type 1 Diabetes
text:
This research project investigates how stress on insulin-producing beta cells leads to the formation of hybrid
insulin peptides (HIPs), which may trigger the autoimmune response in type 1 diabetes (T1D). By studying how
various stressors affect HIP production and how these HIPs interact with the immune system, we aim to uncover
new insights into the development and progression of T1D. Our findings could lead to improved methods for
predicting, preventing, and treating T1D, potentially transforming the management of this chronic autoimmune
disease and improving the lives of millions affected by it.

title: Translation Kinetics and their Effects on Protein Structure and Function, mRNA half-lives, and Cellular Phenotype
text:
Narrative statement
Synonymous mutations, which change the rate at which a codon position is translated by the
ribosome but not the amino acid it encodes, can alter protein structure and function, affect mRNA
half-lives, and contribute to disease. Molecular modeling, interpretable machine learning, and
synthesizing big biological datasets are suggesting molecular mechanisms that can connect this class
of mutations to these outcomes. This research proposal will utilize these tools and experimental
methods to gain quantitative molecular insights into these phenomena.

title: In utero intervention to prevent adverse metabolic health
text:
The proposed research will investigate fetal growth restriction-associated developmental programming in fetal
liver and kidney with and without treatment of the placenta with a nanoparticle gene therapy, and explore the
impact on offspring liver and kidney physiology/function and health in early adulthood.

title: Molecular imaging of RIPK1/necroptosis as a key biomarker in Alzheimer's disease
text:
Receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1) are involved in many human diseases. However, the
RIPK1 expression in the living human brain is poorly understood. This proposal aims to validate a new in vivo
imaging biomarker for directly probing RIPK1 using PET and perform the first-in-human PET imaging. This will
accelerate RIPK1 research and the discovery of RIPK1 therapeutics, which may be used to treat several
human diseases.

title: Multimodal Nanoparticles for Severe Inflammation and Sepsis
text:
Sepsis remains an undrugged disease, largely because current treatment strategies have failed to move
beyond the conventional single-agent, single-target approach. This proposal aims to develop and
mechanistically study a new class of multimodal ‘drug-free’ nanoparticle immunotherapies that augment innate
immunity to overcome the multifaceted immunological deficits that develop during sepsis. If successful, this
approach has the potential to herald a simple and clinically translatable solution to improve patient outcomes
and survival in sepsis.

title: Targeting Ferroptosis in Lethal RB1 Deficient Prostate Cancer
text:
Loss of RB function is a dominant mechanism driving prostate cancer lethality. It is therefore critical to identify
potential therapeutic strategies targeting this disease mechanism to reduce prostate cancer mortality rates and
improve the well-being of patients and their families who are experiencing the impact of the disease. Our work
will delineate downstream effectors of the RB/E2F pathway and provide novel insights into the contributions of
RB to ferroptosis as well as the preclinical data regarding efficacy, safety, and biomarkers required for the rational
design of future clinical trials targeting ferroptosis as a therapeutic approach to treating lethal RB1-deficient
prostate cancer.

title: Improving dermatology access by direct-to-patient teledermatology and computer-assisted diagnosis
text:
Veterans must often wait and travel significant distances to receive care from a VA dermatologist. Emerging
innovative technologies promise to allow VA to deliver expert skin care to Veterans wherever and whenever
they need it. By moving Veterans’ images and histories instead of people, skin concerns can be more rapidly
diagnosed and managed remotely by a dermatologist or eventually by a computer trained by artificial
intelligence methods. This project will implement a VA-developed teledermatology mobile application at three
VA facilities and measure its ability to deliver dermatologic care directly to Veterans in a timely and travel-
minimizing manner, and patient and VA staff satisfaction with the process. In parallel, the project will use the
data that Veteran patients submit to train and refine artificial intelligence-powered computer vision models
whose performance will be tested against dermatologists. The readiness of Veterans and VA to implement
these technologies will also be evaluated.

title: Translation Regulation Contributes to Hypoxia Adaptation in Glioblastoma
text:
Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly malignant primary brain tumor and with a median survival of 15 months despite
aggressive surgical and chemotherapeutic interventions. Glioblastoma stem-like cells (GSCs) are the key cells
responsible for initiating this tumor and they can adapt to the complex environment in the brain, even areas of
low oxygen. This project will help us develop a deeper understanding of GSC biology, especially the tools of
translation regulation (mRNA-to-protein), as they are corrupted for use in stressful low-oxygen conditions
thereby revealing a novel list of targets for future therapy in GBM patients.

title: Molecular Epidemiology in Children's Environmental Health Training Program (MECEH)
text:
There has been an increasing national awareness of the rising number of environmentally-related diseases
such as diabetes, obesity, asthma, neurodevelopmental disorders, and prematurity, among others. The
Molecular Epidemiology in Children's Environmental Health (MECEH) Training Program fills a critical need in
public health by providing future researchers and clinicians with multidisciplinary knowledge and training in
leading and cutting-edge methodologies in the area of pediatric environmental health.

title: Resistance Exercise to Treat Major Depression via Cerebrovascular Mechanisms: Confirming Efficacy and Informing Precision Medicine
text:
Depression is a leading cause of disability worldwide and current treatments, such as psychotherapy and
medication, are ineffective for many people, leading to a high global burden of depression. This project will
investigate the efficacy of a 16-week Resistance Exercise Training (RET) program for treatment of Major
Depressive Disorder via improving cerebrovascular mechanisms and using machine learning to inform future
precision medicine approaches by modeling changes in depression outcomes, cerebrovascular function, and
variation in adherence. If efficacy is confirmed, this highly translatable, accessible, low-cost treatment would
add a novel behavioral treatment option for MDD while the machine learning modeling will independently help
to improve treatment prescription and optimization for people with depression and other serious mental
illnesses.

title: Classification and Prognostication in Pulmonary Thromboembolism Using Computed Tomography Image Analytics
text:
Pulmonary thromboembolism remains a major cause of death and illness in the western world and while
treatment leads to resolution in some, many continue to have symptoms and some develop pulmonary
hypertension, an elevation of the pressures of the lung circulation leading to heart failure. Computed
Tomography (CT imaging is integral to the diagnosis of pulmonary thromboembolism and is routinely obtained
as part of its work-up. In this study we propose to use novel quantitative imaging tools to characterize the lung
and heart in patients with pulmonary thromboembolism to improve identification of chronicity, prognostication
and prediction of response to treatment while at the same time developing a quantitative relationship between
structural changes on imaging and functional impairment.

title: Development of enzymatic tools for rapid measurement of Advanced Glycation and Lipoxidation End Product-protein adducts
text:
Advanced glycation/lipoxidation endproducts (AGE/ALEs) play an important role in diverse age-related
diseases, however no methods exist for rapid, quantitative measurement of AGEs. Development of an
accurate, convenient, and inexpensive method for measuring AGE/ALEs would democratize the tools used to
study AGE/ALEs and be an enabling technology for scientific and clinical research. Here, Revel
Pharmaceuticals is developing rapid, one-pot, inexpensive enzymatic tests to measure important AGEs in
aging and diabetes.

title: The National Center for Interventional Biophotonic Technologies (NCIBT)
text:
The National Center for Interventional Biophotonic Technologies (NCIBT) will promote public health by
improving the clinical management of a broad range of common human conditions, including cancer, stroke,
heart disease, high risk pregnancy, and dementia. Its advanced optical imaging devices will better characterize
tissue structure and function and its AI-based analytical intraprocedural platform will integrate these imaging
data and other patient-specific information into algorithms guiding treatment decisions. The availability of such
helpful guidance as procedures are being performed or critical decisions are being made should help physicians
make better choices that lead to improved patient outcomes.
